description: Every Bitcoin Universe product with its role, documentation home, and source repository. Which protocols a product supports is not stated here; it is derived from capability-snapshot.json so that product pages and the Protocol Atlas can never disagree.

products.name: Core
products.tagline: Explore the chain, hold a portfolio, and trade digital artifacts in one place.
products.role: The explorer, portfolio, and marketplace application. Core is where assets are discovered, inspected, and traded, and it is the surface most protocol support is measured against.

products.name: Wallet
products.tagline: Self-custody for Bitcoin digital artifacts, with approvals you can actually read.
products.role: The browser wallet. It holds keys, separates payment outputs from asset-bearing outputs, and presents what a signature authorises before it is given.

products.name: Inscribe
products.tagline: Create on Bitcoin: files, text, tokens, and collections, with the cost shown before you commit.
products.role: The creation studio. Inscribe builds the transactions that bring new artifacts and tokens into existence, across every protocol whose creation path is implemented.

products.name: StampDEX
products.tagline: A trading venue for Bitcoin Stamps and SRC-20.
products.role: The Stamps marketplace surface, with its own order and settlement model distinct from the Core marketplace.

products.name: Zerdinals and Z-Runes
products.tagline: Digital artifacts and fungible tokens native to Zcash.
products.role: The Zcash application and its protocol family, including the ZordiScan explorer, with explicit treatment of transparent and shielded activity.

products.name: Forked Felines
products.tagline: A collection held whole on Bitcoin.
products.role: The collection: artwork, traits, provenance, minting, and the collector experience around it.

products.name: Drops
products.tagline: Permanent media and agreements on an original carrier.
products.role: The Drops application and the OP_DROP carrier beneath it, including Drop Pacts.
